depth_m.quote: CJPL-I was built under Jinping Mountain with 2,400 m of rock overburden.

geometry.locator: Section II: "The distances to the east and west ends of the tunnel entrance are 8.7 km and 8.8 km, respectively."
geometry.note: Point stands in for the ~6.5 m x 6.5 m x 40 m main hall; not a trace of the hall's own footprint (no plan giving that footprint's orientation along the tunnel axis was found; checked 2026-09-18).
geometry.quote: Construction of Phase I of CJPL (CJPL-I) started in December 2009 near the center of one of the Jinping traffic tunnels, where the vertical rock overburden is maximal ... The distances to the east and west ends of the tunnel entrance are 8.7 km and 8.8 km, respectively.

method: Walked along the Jinping traffic tunnel (OSM ways 681216327 and 653641019, the twin bores) from both portals, using the distances CJPL's own review paper states: 8.8 km from the west portal and 8.7 km from the east portal to CJPL-I's main hall. This gives four independent point estimates (2 bores x 2 directions of measurement); they agree to within 6-81 m of their centroid (mean pairwise spread ~39 m), which is used here as the coordinate. This is anchored entirely on the OSM tunnel line (accuracy 25 m) and the paper's own portal distances, not on any earlier site-level campus point, so it does not rest on a coarser anchor than its own stated accuracy. The tunnel-derived point sits 124 m from the campus-grade geocoder point already on record for this site (well inside that point's own precision): consistent, not a contradiction.
name: CJPL-I main hall (derived point, walked along the traffic tunnel)

summary.plain: CJPL-I's main experimental hall, located by walking the sourced 8.7-8.8 km portal distances along the OpenStreetMap trace of the Jinping traffic tunnel.
